pages.alt: A right-angled triangle with a square drawn on each side. Its shorter sides are 4 centimetres and 3 centimetres. The square on the 4 centimetre side holds 16 unit squares and the square on the 3 centimetre side holds 9. The 16 move into the corner of the square on the longest side, and the 9 fill the rest of it exactly. 16 plus 9 equals 25 unit squares.

pages.name: The biggest square
pages.task: In this right-angled triangle, the squares on the shorter sides cover 64 cm² and 36 cm². How much does the square on the longest side cover?
pages.why: The pieces of the two smaller squares fill the square on the longest side exactly. So it covers 64 + 36 = 100 cm².
pages.alt: A right-angled triangle with a square drawn on each side. The square on the 8 centimetre side covers 64 square centimetres and the square on the 6 centimetre side covers 36. The area of the square on the longest side is not shown. The unit squares of both smaller squares move into it and fill it exactly: 64 plus 36 equals 100 square centimetres.

pages.name: The hypotenuse
pages.text: The longest side, opposite the right angle, is the [[hypotenuse]]. Its square holds 25 unit squares, 5 along each edge, so the side is √25 = 5 cm.

pages.name: Find the hypotenuse
pages.task: A right-angled triangle's shorter sides are 12 cm and 5 cm. How long is its hypotenuse?
pages.why: Square the shorter sides and add. 144 + 25 = 169 cm² is the hypotenuse's square, and the square root undoes the square, so the hypotenuse is √169 = 13 cm.

The squares cover 144 square centimetres, 25 square centimetres, 169 square centimetres, and the side asked for is the square root of 169, 13 centimetres.

pages.name: A shorter side
pages.text: For a shorter side, take away. The hypotenuse's square holds 100, so 100 − 36 = 64 are left, an 8 by 8 square. The side is √64 = 8 cm.
pages.alt: A right-angled triangle with a square drawn on each side. Its hypotenuse is 10 centimetres, one shorter side is 6 centimetres, and the other is not known. The square on the hypotenuse holds 100 unit squares. 36 of them move back to the square on the 6 centimetre side, and the 8 by 8 block of 64 that is left moves to the third side. 100 minus 36 equals 64, and the square root of 64 is 8, so the third side is 8 centimetres.

pages.name: Which side?
pages.task: This right-angled triangle has sides of 15 cm and 9 cm. How long is the third side?
pages.why: The 15 cm side is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse. Take away, 225 − 81 = 144 cm², and √144 = 12 cm.

pages.name: Make it fit
pages.task: This triangle's base is 8 cm. Drag the top corner so the hypotenuse is 10 cm.
pages.why: The hypotenuse's square is 10² = 100 and the base's is 8² = 64, leaving 36 for the upright side. √36 = 6, so the corner goes 6 cm up.

pages.task: These 4 cm and 3 cm sides meet at a corner narrower than a right angle. How long is the third side?
pages.why: Pythagoras only works with a right angle. A narrower corner brings the ends closer, so the third side is less than 5 cm and the 25 unit squares spill over.

The squares on the two sides hold 16 and 9 unit squares; the third side is not labelled. The 25 unit squares move into the square on the third side and spill over its edges, so the third side is less than 5 centimetres.

pages.name: A right angle?
pages.task: A triangle's sides are 8 cm, 7 cm and 11 cm. Is the corner between the 8 cm and 7 cm sides a right angle?
pages.why: 8² + 7² = 64 + 49 = 113, but 11² = 121 is more. So the corner is wider than a right angle, and the 113 unit squares leave a gap.
pages.alt: A triangle with sides of 8 centimetres, 7 centimetres and 11 centimetres, a square on each side, and unit squares on the two shorter sides' squares. The corner between the 8 and 7 centimetre sides looks close to a right angle. The 64 and 49 unit squares move into the 11 centimetre side's square of 121 and leave 8 places empty, outlined, so the corner is wider than a right angle.

pages.name: A shelf bracket
pages.task: A shelf bracket's two arms meet at a right angle and are 20 cm and 30 cm long. How long is the brace between their ends?
pages.why: The brace is opposite the right angle, so it is the hypotenuse. 20² + 30² = 400 + 900 = 1,300 cm², and √1,300 = 36.06 cm, to 2 decimal places.
